original_question: Let Z be the Cantor-like space of nondecreasing functions f in N^(N ∪ {∞}) such that whenever f(n) < ∞ one has f(n) < f(n+1), let Q be the dense set of eventually-∞ sequences q_s coming from increasing finite sequences s, let B = {f_α : α < b} be a <=*-unbounded b-scale of strictly increasing functions in N^N, and let H = B ∪ Q. Must H satisfy S_1(Γ, Γ), that is, for every sequence of open γ-covers of H can one choose one element from each cover so that the chosen family is again a γ-cover of H?
target_in_paper: §6.1, Problem 3 ([6, Problem 17]): for the set H = B ∪ Q constructed from a 𝔟-scale inside Z, does H satisfy S1(Γ, Γ)?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper-faithful target. It correctly identifies the same ambient construction Z, the dense set Q of eventually-∞ sequences q_s, a 𝔟-scale B of strictly increasing functions, the set H = B ∪ Q, and the exact property being asked about: whether H satisfies S1(Γ, Γ). This matches the open problem stated in §6.1 as Problem 3.
missing_details: The topology on N ∪ {∞} should be specified: it is the one-point compactification of N, and Z is a subspace of (N ∪ {∞})^N with the product topology.
It should be stated that B ⊆ N^N is viewed as a subset of Z via the functions that never take the value ∞, so H is a subspace of Z.
The paper's convention for 'cover' is nontrivial: if 𝒰 is a cover of H, then H = ⋃𝒰 and H is not itself a member of 𝒰.
The meaning of a γ-cover should be made explicit in the stand-alone question: it is an infinite open cover in which each point belongs to all but finitely many members.
The phrase 'Must H satisfy' should be made explicit as a ZFC/unconditional question: for every such 𝔟-scale B, does the resulting H have the property?
To match the paper's setup exactly, the open γ-covers are taken with respect to the subspace topology on H inherited from Z.
refined_question: In ZFC, let N ∪ {∞} be the one-point compactification of N, and let Z ⊆ (N ∪ {∞})^N be the subspace of all functions f such that f(n) ≤ f(n+1) for every n and, whenever f(n) < ∞, one has f(n) < f(n+1). For each increasing finite sequence s ∈ N^{<ω}, define q_s ∈ Z by q_s(k) = s(k) for k < |s| and q_s(k) = ∞ for k ≥ |s|, and let Q = {q_s : s is an increasing finite sequence}. If B = {f_α : α < 𝔟} ⊆ N^N is a 𝔟-scale of strictly increasing functions (that is, B is <=*-unbounded and α < β implies f_α <=* f_β), viewed as a subset of Z, and H = B ∪ Q, must H satisfy S1(Γ, Γ)? Equivalently: for every sequence (𝒰_n) of open γ-covers of H in the subspace topology from Z, where a γ-cover means an infinite nontrivial open cover in which each x ∈ H belongs to all but finitely many members, can one choose U_n ∈ 𝒰_n for each n so that {U_n : n ∈ N} is again a γ-cover of H?
justification: The draft is targeting the specific problem in §6.1, not the earlier classification problems: the construction of Z, Q, B, and H appears there, and the paper then asks exactly whether H satisfies S1(Γ, Γ). The formal definition of S1(Γ, Γ) comes from §2.1 together with the definition of γ-cover in §3, and Figure 1 identifies S1(Γ, Γ) with the classical γ-set property. The only substantive additions needed are the ambient topology and the paper's conventions about covers.
